strings.d1.s0.name: Edinburgh Castle
strings.d1.s0.tips: A fortress on a volcanic rock: the Scottish Crown Jewels, the Stone of Destiny and the 13:00 one o'clock gun. Book timed tickets online, as they sell out.
strings.d1.s1.name: Royal Mile Walk
strings.d1.s1.tips: 1.6 km from the castle to Holyrood. Take in St Giles' Cathedral (Thistle Chapel) and the closes (narrow alleys), and join a Mary King's Close tour.
strings.d1.s2.name: Deacon Brodie's Tavern
strings.d1.s2.tips: Named after the thieving councillor who inspired Dr Jekyll. Try haggis, neeps and tatties.
strings.d1.s3.name: The Real Mary King's Close
strings.d1.s3.tips: Buried 17th-century streets beneath the road, with tales of the plague. Book ahead.
strings.d1.s4.name: Scotch Whisky Experience
strings.d1.s4.tips: A barrel ride and a tasting, plus a collection of 3,000 bottles. On Castlehill.
strings.d1.b0.name: Oink Victoria Street
strings.d1.b0.tips: Hog roast sandwiches. Expect a queue.
strings.d1.b1.name: Camera Obscura
strings.d1.b1.tips: An illusion tower from 1835. A swap for Mary King's Close if you have children.
strings.d2.s0.name: Arthur's Seat
strings.d2.s0.tips: An extinct volcano, 251 m high. 45 minutes from Holyrood Park, with panoramic views of the city and the Firth of Forth. Expect wind.
strings.d2.s1.name: Palace of Holyroodhouse
strings.d2.s1.tips: The monarch's palace in Scotland. See Mary, Queen of Scots' rooms and the ruined abbey.
strings.d2.s2.name: The Sheep Heid Inn
strings.d2.s2.tips: Scotland's oldest pub, dating from 1360 (a queen once visited). It has a skittles alley and a village setting in Duddingston.
strings.d2.s3.name: Calton Hill
strings.d2.s3.tips: The National Monument (an unfinished Parthenon) and the Nelson Monument. The best postcard view of the city, especially at sunset.
strings.d2.s4.name: Dean Village
strings.d2.s4.tips: A medieval milling village on the Water of Leith. A fairy tale within the city.
strings.d2.b0.name: Dynamic Earth
strings.d2.b0.tips: A science centre telling the history of the planet. A swap for Holyrood if you have children.
strings.d2.b1.name: Holyrood 9A
strings.d2.b1.tips: Burgers and craft beer, just off the Royal Mile.
strings.d3.s0.name: National Gallery of Scotland
strings.d3.s0.tips: Free, on the Mound. See Titian, Raeburn's The Skating Minister and The Monarch of the Glen.
strings.d3.s1.name: Princes Street Gardens & Scott Monument
strings.d3.s1.tips: A Gothic rocket of a monument with 287 steps. The gardens look up to the castle and have a floral clock.
strings.d3.s2.name: Stockbridge Market & Circus Lane
strings.d3.s2.tips: The market runs on Sundays. Circus Lane is a flower-lined back street, popular for photos.
strings.d3.s3.name: The Scran & Scallie
strings.d3.s3.tips: Tom Kitchin's gastropub, serving Scottish produce.
strings.d3.s4.name: Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh
strings.d3.s4.tips: A botanic garden founded in 1670. The glasshouses are ticketed, and Inverleith Hill has views of the castle.
strings.d3.b0.name: Scottish National Portrait Gallery
strings.d3.b0.tips: A neo-Gothic red building. Free, with portraits of Mary Stuart.
strings.d3.b1.name: The Pantry
strings.d3.b1.tips: Brunch in Stockbridge. Expect a queue.
strings.d4.s0.name: Rosslyn Chapel
strings.d4.s0.tips: The 1446 chapel from The Da Vinci Code. See the Apprentice Pillar and hundreds of carvings. Take the 37 bus, 40 minutes.
strings.d4.s1.name: Roslin Glen Walk
strings.d4.s1.tips: A stream valley below the chapel, with castle ruins.
strings.d4.s2.name: The Original Rosslyn Inn
strings.d4.s3.name: Flotterstone, Pentland Hills
strings.d4.s3.tips: Hills south of the city. Walk to Glencorse Reservoir past grazing sheep. Take the 101 bus.
strings.d4.b0.name: Craigmillar Castle
strings.d4.b0.tips: A ruined castle where Mary Stuart took refuge. Inside the city, so a swap for the Pentlands.
strings.d4.b1.name: Flotterstone Inn
strings.d4.b1.tips: A pub at the entrance to the Pentlands.
strings.d5.s0.name: Stirling Castle
strings.d5.s0.tips: 50 minutes by train. The castle of the Scottish kings, with the Great Hall and views of the Wallace Monument.
strings.d5.s1.name: National Wallace Monument
strings.d5.s1.tips: A 67 m tower to the Braveheart hero, marking the Battle of Stirling Bridge (1297). 246 steps.
strings.d5.s2.name: Stirling Old Town Lunch
strings.d5.s2.tips: A café beside the Old Town Jail. Try the Cullen skink soup.
strings.d5.s3.name: Balloch, Loch Lomond
strings.d5.s3.tips: 1 hour by tour or train. Scotland's largest loch, with Balloch Castle park and boat trips (summer).
strings.d5.s4.name: Luss
strings.d5.s4.tips: A stone village on the loch shore. Watch the sunset from the pier (by tour or car).
strings.d5.b0.name: Doune Castle
strings.d5.b0.tips: The castle of Monty Python and Outlander. A swap for the Wallace Monument (by car).
strings.d5.b1.name: The Portcullis
strings.d5.b1.tips: A pub at the castle gate in Stirling.
strings.d6.s0.name: Royal Yacht Britannia
strings.d6.s0.tips: The Queen's yacht from 1953 to 1997. At Leith's Ocean Terminal, with an audio guide.
strings.d6.s1.name: The Shore, Leith
strings.d6.s1.tips: The old harbour. This is the Trainspotting district, with Michelin-starred restaurants.
strings.d6.s2.name: Fishers Leith
strings.d6.s2.tips: Seafood in the harbour tower. Open since 1991.
strings.d6.s3.name: Water of Leith Walkway
strings.d6.s3.tips: A 5 km riverside path from Leith to Dean Village, passing Antony Gormley statues in the water.
strings.d6.s4.name: Surgeons' Hall Museums
strings.d6.s4.tips: A surgical museum covering the body snatchers Burke and Hare. Only if you have a strong stomach.
strings.d6.b0.name: The Kitchin
strings.d6.b0.tips: Michelin-starred. Lunch menu, so book ahead.
strings.d6.b1.name: Portobello Beach
strings.d6.b1.tips: A city beach with a Victorian promenade. A swap for Leith.
strings.d7.s0.name: Greyfriars Kirkyard
strings.d7.s0.tips: The statue of Greyfriars Bobby the dog. Harry Potter names appear on the gravestones (Tom Riddle).
strings.d7.s1.name: The Elephant House Breakfast
strings.d7.s1.tips: The café where Rowling wrote (now reopened). The back room has views of the castle.
strings.d7.s2.name: National Museum of Scotland
strings.d7.s2.tips: Dolly the sheep and the Lewis chessmen. Free, with a roof terrace.
strings.d7.s3.name: Waverley Tram to the Airport
strings.d7.s3.tips: 35 minutes to the airport by tram. Farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Mums Great Comfort Food
strings.d7.b0.tips: On Forrest Road. Sausages and mash.
strings.d7.b1.name: Grassmarket Saturday Market
strings.d7.b1.tips: A farmers' and crafts market on Saturdays.
strings.note0: A Lothian bus day ticket costs 5.50 GBP (via the app) and the airport tram 7 GBP. Take the train to Stirling and Loch Lomond, and the 37 bus to Rosslyn. The city is hilly but walkable.
strings.note1: August brings the Fringe and Tattoo festivals (3,000 shows). Hotels cost three times as much, so book months ahead. Summer is 15-20°C with changeable weather, and daylight lasts until 22:00. June and July are ideal.
strings.note2: The castle costs 20 GBP and online tickets are mandatory. The museums (National, Galleries) are free. A pub lunch costs 15-20 GBP, a whisky tasting 25 GBP, and a tip is 10%.
strings.note3: Try haggis, Cullen skink, Scotch pie, cranachan and Irn-Bru. For whisky, Islay is smoky and Speyside is sweet.
strings.note4: You can get four seasons in an hour: carry a raincoat and dress in layers. The wind is fierce on Calton Hill and Arthur's Seat.
strings.note5: Harry Potter spots: Victoria Street, Greyfriars, the Elephant House, and room 552 at the Balmoral Hotel.
